subject: social
source: CISCE Curriculum for Primary Classes I-V (2016), official

covers: Compare nuclear, joint and single-parent families
Share how their family, neighbourhood and surroundings have changed
Compare how food, homes, clothes, transport and entertainment have changed over time
Think and talk fairly about gender roles in work and play
Draw a timeline of family members' birthdays
Name and list important holidays and festivals
Put events in order on a calendar and timeline, and know the idea of AD and BC
Adjust to a change such as moving home or school
Name community helpers such as soldiers, farmers, teachers, doctors, police and firefighters, and what each one does
See how people in a community depend on each other
Respect all kinds of work and the dignity of labour
Show care for old, sick, needy and differently abled people
Thank school support staff and domestic workers
Take part in a cleanliness drive
Feel empathy by imagining another child's life, such as a rag picker's
Follow safety rules at home, in school and on the road
Use everyday objects such as knives, irons and gadgets safely
Use phones, tablets and the internet safely, with an adult
Know and obey basic road signs, signals and walking and cycling rules
Know basic first aid and emergency numbers such as 101, 102 and 103
Tell a good touch from a bad touch
Recognise bullying and speak up about it

topics.topic: India- A Land of Rich Heritage
covers: Understand what heritage is and why it matters
Name important buildings, monuments and national symbols
Know great national leaders and what they achieved
Retell stories from epics and folk tales such as the Panchatantra and Jataka tales
List national and local festivals and take part in them respectfully
Feel pride in the country's art, traditions and culture
Know that the Earth is a planet in the solar system
Name the Sun, planets, satellites and stars
Explain what makes the Earth unique, such as air, water and its distance from the Sun
Know the shape of the Earth
Tell a globe (a 3D model of the Earth) from a map (a 2D picture of the Earth)
Compare physical and political maps
Use directions and a compass
Explain what the environment is and why cleanliness matters
Name the three main kinds of pollution: air, water and noise
Find causes and effects of each kind of pollution
Understand the importance of trees and green belts, through the Chipko movement and Van Mahotsav
Take part in tree planting and cleanliness drives
Build healthy habits that protect the environment
